title: The case system in extended sentences
prior_teaching_boundary: Only actual reviewed Units1–9 form, sense and construction milestones count. Earlier supplied reading frames and instrumental references require explicit promotion or local support. Preserve every earlier identity, analysis and history.
productive_outcomes: Distinguish a complete noun phrase’s externally governed case from its internal dependent genitive; use selected verbs with genitive objects and dative person/genitive thing.
Use bounded nominal partitives with ān, sum and hwilc and fela with genitive plural, keeping these distinct from agreeing numerals and attributive adjectives.

Distinguish ordinary dative recipient/beneficiary/governed-person uses from bounded ðyncan with dative experiencer and nominative subject, and hyngran with accusative experiencer and a third-singular impersonal verb.
Express selected means by mid plus dative or by the bare instrumental; use explicitly promoted masculine/neuter singular instrumental determiner/adjective forms and explain syncretism.

Use full assigned exceptional fæder, hand and gāt noun systems and complete nominal/adjectival morphology within its stated lexical, number and syntactic limits; familiar classes have actual printed models and explicit diagnostic rows.

Use complete defined new verbal systems with all endings, stem changes, exceptions and scope boundaries; preserve unnan’s unsupported present2sg gap and use the evidenced subjunctive command substitute.

Use explicitly assigned source lexical frames, object descriptions, substantival adjectives, temporal questions, destination, right/left-side idiom, hearing/perception and selected future-reference contexts without generalizing whole later clause systems.
Complete all55 unchanged Cook III.13–15 prompts and34 purposeful original tasks; read the50word new account independently and the59word exact Judgment tableau with its approved local support.
recognition_outcomes: Recognize documented variants and reference-only number, adjective and instrumental cells without inferring productive syntax from their display.
Distinguish the exact source forms, connective senses, elliptical predicates, quality genitive, passive, comparison and division/placement expressions through printed support.
Recognize evidence limits in defective verbal cells, source ambiguity and original apparatus; correct Cook153d’s analysis while preserving its wording.
bounded_scope: Complete morphology does not promote unassigned syntax or number senses.
Crīst has only four singular proper-name cells; dōm/rēaf/woruld plural cells remain recognition within assigned senses.
New adjective instrumental cells remain recognition; only selected earlier demonstrative and gōd instrumental cells receive productive means scope.
No broad subjunctive, oblique-case, passive, future, preposition or impersonal grammar is inferred from local helps.
Unnan has no evidenced present indicative second-singular cell and no separately asserted formal imperative; supported subjunctives supply the command.
The 59-word exact reading ends before royal speech; all nine helps and fourteen original notes remain available.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Fæder is masculine; selected endingless genitive/dative singular fæder, with fæderes/fædere accepted; plural follows fæderas/fædera/fæderum/fæderas. Cook43.8 gives an exception to the strong masculine system, not an instruction to derive an umlaut dat singular.

Gāt: N/A singular gāt, selected G singular gāte (variant gǣt), D singular gǣt (variant gāte); N/A plural gǣt, G plural gāta, D plural gātum. The long vowel alternation is ā/ǣ; no -as plural or fictitious gǣtum.

Hand/woruld use strong feminine morphology with endingless accusative singular. Cook p297 explicitly directs hand to51.1.3; this lexical cross-reference licenses51.1 even though hand is absent from its exemplar list. Selected genitive/dative hande/worulde; source-authorized -a variants are accepted. A syncretic adjective ending alone does not disambiguate hand phrases.

Selected dryhten/dēofol/ęngel retain full nominative/accusative singular but use dryhtn-/dēofl-/ęngl- with endings; stem diagnostics control every cell. Compounds giesthūs and cweartern retain their terminal noun stems.

Apply complete prior strong/weak adjective systems. Retained-vowel disyllables, -e adjectives, long-stem unrihtwīs and double-consonant synfull have explicit diagnostics; swīðra has weak comparative morphology only. Displayed instrumental forms remain recognition unless the coordinator names an explicit productive means frame.

Hungry, sick, naked and unrighteous adjectives can name persons in the weak declension; the new people senses are separately assigned. Their case is governed by the containing clause, not by English the.

audited_inflection_rules.title: Selected weakI systems
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Present -e/-st/-ð/-að with selected contractions; past -e/-est/-e/-on added to the checked dental past stem. Long vowel+d gives dd in fēdde, scrȳdde, tōgelǣdde. Scęnc- takes -te, forwiern- -de.
audited_inflection_rules.variants: Cook permits tt/t contraction. BT explicitly attests fēt/fētt/fēdeð; selected production target fēt. Uncontracted and alternative spelling forms are not independently new recall targets.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Only declared indicative cells and separately listed complete command pairs; citations are supplied, not automatic infinitive production.

audited_inflection_rules.title: Selected weakII systems
audited_inflection_rules.rule: -ie, -ast, -að, plural -iað; preterite -ode, -odest, -ode, plural -odon. Command genēosa/genēosiað. Retain Cook longē in genēos-.
audited_inflection_rules.variants: Cook records plural -edon beside -odon, ig(e)/g beside i in endings, and alternate past vowels; -odon and i are the selected productive forms. Alternative weakI andswerian remains unassigned.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: No regular weakII rule licenses another verb’s lexical case frame.

audited_inflection_rules.title: Gewītan strongI
audited_inflection_rules.rule: ī present, ā first/third singular past, short i second singular/plural past; t-stem contractions yield gewītst/gewīt. Select gewāt/gewite/gewiton.
audited_inflection_rules.variants: Final tt beside t is source-rule supported; selected short t. Optional reflexive dative is attested, not obligatory in the chosen departure frame.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Do not confuse with gewitan know.

audited_inflection_rules.title: Supported unnan system
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Indicative ann/unnon; past ūðe/ūðest/ūðe/ūðon; subjunctive unne/unnen and ūðe/ūðen, all persons. Present indicative2sg visibly has no assigned form. Direct addressed command uses second-person unne/unnen.
audited_inflection_rules.variants: Cook an(n) permits an and ann; selected ann. Cook labels unne imperative; Fulk describes subjunctive substitution. Both source descriptions are preserved.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: No invented anst/unnest/unne indicative2sg or unnað formal imperative. The omission records checked-source limits, not universal nonattestation.

audited_inflection_rules.title: Two bounded experiencer systems
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Hyngreð/hyngrede with accusative experiencer and no expressed nominative; ðyncð/ðūhte with dative experiencer and a singular neuter nominative stimulus. Each defined finite system has exactly present3sg and past3sg.
audited_inflection_rules.variants: Other personal and case frames are documented but not assigned; source quantity/spelling is explicit.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: No fabricated personal paradigm for the subjectless frame; no promotion of Unit9 entire passive/judgment construction.

audited_inflection_rules.title: Case form and contextual role
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Se has masculine/neuter singular ðȳ (variant ðon); strong gōd has gōde in those cells. Nouns, feminine singular and plural express this relation with dative-shaped forms. The food noun retains mete-dat-sg canonical identity; context marks instrumental function.
audited_inflection_rules.variants: Prose mid+DAT ordinary; bare means more characteristic of poetry. Do not assign Anglian mid+distinct instrumental as the normal EWS production choice.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: All six newly promoted distinct cells are displayed; earlier ðes/hwā instruments remain recognition-only.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-fedan-commands
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Both singular and plural commands of fēdan.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-scrydan-commands
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Both singular and plural commands of scrȳdan.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-geneosian-commands
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Both singular and plural commands of genēosian.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-wyrcean-commands
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Both singular and plural commands of wyrcean.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-genitive-relations
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Bounded adnominal genitive: possession/kinship, origin or belonging, and the agent or object relation to a verbal noun; the dependent genitive retains its own case inside an externally governed head phrase.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Cook §153d incorrectly names ęgesan rather than Frēan as objective genitive; preserve the printed text and correct the analysis.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-genitive-quality-source
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Recognize source setle his mægenðrymnesse: genitive of quality, naturally throne of his glory.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Source-bound quality construction, not independent free productive abstract-genitive composition.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-partitive-group
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Substantival ān, sum and hwilc may select a genitive count group; the group stays genitive while the head has the case required by its clause.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Contrast attributive ān agreeing with a singular noun. No unbounded quantity syntax.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-fela-genitive
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Invariant fela takes genitive plural for the selected many/count-group frame.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Do not infer micel +mass or general noun-of-measure syntax.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-governed-case-contrast
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Choose case by the checked lexical frame: helpan+dative, geswīcan/gīeman+genitive, and new unnan/forwiernan+dative person+genitive thing.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: English object position does not decide Old English case; each lexical frame has separate evidence.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-unnan-government
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Unnan grants a genitive thing to a dative person.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-forwiernan-government
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Forwiernan refuses a genitive thing to a dative person.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-dative-roles
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Distinguish recipient, lexically governed person, beneficiary and experiencer. A shared dative form does not make the roles identical.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Only separately documented lexical and prepositional frames are productive.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-present-future
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Present indicative can refer to future events where context supplies futurity; English will/shall need not produce willan.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Willan remains volitional where intention is meant; no new periphrastic future tense.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-to-destination
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Tō+dative gives a destination with come/go/fly.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Separate from tō purpose/function and tō+inflected infinitive.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-on-side-idiom
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Bounded on ... hand uses accusative in the right/left-hand expression, including attested static standan.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Bare hand supports accusative; weak swīðran alone is case-ambiguous. Ordinary on+dative location remains available; Cook warns rest/motion distinction is not invariant.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-on-name-idiom
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Bounded on+genitive possessor+naman expresses in someone’s name; naman is dative and the internal possessor genitive.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-beforan-location
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Beforan+dative person expresses standing before/in front of someone.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Explicit promotion of prior source-only exposure.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-perception-object-predicate
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Gesēon takes an accusative object with an agreeing accusative adjective describing its perceived condition.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: E.g. hungry/sick; do not convert it into the distinct accusative+infinitive frame.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-hieran-perception-infinitive
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Hīeran can take an accusative perceived actor with a plain infinitive naming its action.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Explicit lexical extension distinct from prior gesēon frame; no general control/complement syntax.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-substantival-personal-adjectives
audited_inflection_rules.rule: The selected weak adjectives with the article can name people: the hungry, naked, sick, unrighteous; case and number follow their clause role.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Plural people and an adjective modifying an expressed singular person must be distinguished. Do not imply every abstract substantive use is covered.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-fedan-accusative-means
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Fēdan takes accusative being fed; food may be expressed as mid+dative means or bounded bare instrumental means.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Bare food example is new composition derived from independently checked lexical and case rules, not an exact quotation.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-scrydan-accusative
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Scrȳdan clothes an accusative person.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Garment mid+dative is documented reference evidence only; it is not an additional independently assigned lexical complement.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-andswarian-dative
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Andswarian answers a dative addressee, with a following direct quotation if expressed.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-scencan-recipient
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Scęncan pours accusative drink for a dative recipient.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-geneosian-accusative
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Genēosian visits an accusative person in the selected frame.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: BT421 hine examples disambiguate accusative; nēosian genitive government is not denied.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-gewitan-departure
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Gewītan means depart/go away and may take fram+dative source.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Not the distinct short-vowel preterite-present know.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-togelaedan-recipient
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Tōgelǣdan brings an accusative thing to a dative recipient.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Promotes the actually supplied prior frame with full selected indicative morphology.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-don-beneficiary
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Dōn takes an accusative deed/it and dative affected person in the selected do-good-deeds-to frame.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-totwaeman-separation
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Tōtwǣman separates an accusative being/group from a fram+dative other group.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Explicit lexical extension of prior division frame; no new verbal paradigm.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-hwonne-direct-question
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Hwonne introduces a direct when-question using ordinary finite interrogative syntax.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: No temporal subordinate when-clause system is introduced.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-sellan-drink-infinitive
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Supplied sęllan +dative person +plain drincan: give someone to drink.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Local Cook III.14.11 support; not independent recall of a general purpose construction.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-swa-lange-swa-supplied
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Supplied swā lange swā ... expresses as long as / inasmuch as with the stated past actions.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Supply both correlation tokens and lange. Cook p135 note17 explicitly observes inasmuch-as force; do not impose duration. No productive temporal-subordination system.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-coordinated-predicate-ellipsis
audited_inflection_rules.rule: In bounded coordination with two different expressed subjects, recover the omitted repeated predicate from the preceding clause.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Cook III.15.9 morning/night coming; source p134 the angels share the preceding coming predicate. No free deletion rule.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-wyrcean-work
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Wyrcean takes accusative work/deed, including cognate weorc, in the selected work/perform sense.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Distinguish this new ordinary sense from the earlier yield-fruit frame.

audited_inflection_rules.title: u10-promoted-plain-infinitives
audited_inflection_rules.rule: Promote the separately registered cīepan/bycgan plain infinitives for deliberate willan and blāwan for the new hīeran-perception construction.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Only plain-infinitive use in these defined frames. Earlier supplied citation status is preserved historically.

audit_recommendation_precedence: Explicit contract assignments and scope govern. Audit records supply evidence and preserve prior milestones; displaying a cell does not teach every use.

local_support.text: Witodlice is a connective here (Cook gives Latin autem). Mannes Bearn means the Son of Man: mannes is genitive singular and Bearn neuter nominative singular. The subsequent hē/him/his refer to this male person.
In his glory/majesty. Mægenðrymme is dative masculine singular. This abstract expression is supplied as a whole.

local_support.source_expression: and ealle ęnglas samod mid him …
local_support.text: And all the angels together with him. The source leaves the coming verb understood in this coordinated part; the angels are nominative plural, not objects of with. Mid him separately means with him. Tō ðǣm miclan dōme means to the great judgment.
Then. Both occurrences are independent sentence adverbs sequencing the scene; they are not the previously taught than or subordinate when.
Throne/seat of his majesty. Mægenðrymnesse is a feminine genitive singular characterizing the throne; Cook note7 refers to the genitive of quality (§153.f).

local_support.source_expression: bēoð gegaderode ætforan him ealle ðēoda
local_support.text: All nations will be gathered before him. Bēoð is third-person plural, and ðēoda is the following nominative feminine plural subject. Gegaderode is the exact supplied plural passive participle; ætforan him means before him. Ealle is the feminine plural -e variant here; the ordinary selected target ealla remains valid.

Separates them into two groups. Tōscǣt is third-person singular present; hīe is its accusative plural object. On twā is the locally supplied divided-in-two expression; twā is neuter accusative plural here.

local_support.source_expression: swā-swā scēaphierde tōscǣt scēap fram gātum
local_support.text: Just as a shepherd separates sheep from goats. The whole comparative connection is supplied. Scēaphierde is the nominative subject, scēap the accusative plural object, and gātum dative after fram. The noun scēap has identical singular/plural nominative/accusative shapes; the source explicitly identifies this occurrence as plural.

local_support.source_expression: gelōgað … on his swīðran hand … on his winstran
local_support.text: He places the sheep at his right hand and the goats at his left. Gelōgað is an exact supplied third-singular present. The two animal phrases are accusative plural objects. The right/left expressions share a placement frame; on takes accusative hand in this bounded right/left-side expression (the final hand is understood). The following unassigned source line8 uses the same expression with static standað; this is not a universal motion-versus-rest rule. Swīðran/winstran are weak feminine singular forms. Their -an alone does not distinguish accusative from dative; judge the complete clause and the bare hand form.

editorial_lines.text: Witodlice Mannes Bearn cymð on his mægenðrymme,
and ealle ęnglas samod mid him tō ðǣm miclan dōme.
Ðonne sitt hē on ðǣm setle his mægenðrymnesse, and
bēoð gegaderode ætforan him ealle ðēoda, and hē tōscǣt
hīe on twā, swā-swā scēaphierde tōscǣt scēap fram
gātum. Ðonne gelōgað hē ðā scēap on his swīðran
hand, and ðā gǣt on his winstran.

Coordinates the separating clause.
Subject of tōscǣt.
Third singular present separates; exact supplied source verb.
Accusative plural object; refers to all nations/people just gathered.
Into two groups, source construction supplied as a whole.

Introduces the supported as/just-as comparison with a shepherd.
Masculine nominative singular subject inside comparison.
Same exact third singular finite form as token35.

local_support.text: Witodlice is a connective here (Cook gives Latin autem). Mannes Bearn means the Son of Man: mannes is genitive singular and Bearn neuter nominative singular. The subsequent hē/him/his refer to this male person.
In his glory/majesty. Mægenðrymme is dative masculine singular. This abstract expression is supplied as a whole.

local_support.source_expression: and ealle ęnglas samod mid him …
local_support.text: And all the angels together with him. The source leaves the coming verb understood in this coordinated part; the angels are nominative plural, not objects of with. Mid him separately means with him. Tō ðǣm miclan dōme means to the great judgment.
Then. Both occurrences are independent sentence adverbs sequencing the scene; they are not the previously taught than or subordinate when.
Throne/seat of his majesty. Mægenðrymnesse is a feminine genitive singular characterizing the throne; Cook note7 refers to the genitive of quality (§153.f).

local_support.source_expression: bēoð gegaderode ætforan him ealle ðēoda
local_support.text: All nations will be gathered before him. Bēoð is third-person plural, and ðēoda is the following nominative feminine plural subject. Gegaderode is the exact supplied plural passive participle; ætforan him means before him. Ealle is the feminine plural -e variant here; the ordinary selected target ealla remains valid.

Separates them into two groups. Tōscǣt is third-person singular present; hīe is its accusative plural object. On twā is the locally supplied divided-in-two expression; twā is neuter accusative plural here.

local_support.source_expression: swā-swā scēaphierde tōscǣt scēap fram gātum
local_support.text: Just as a shepherd separates sheep from goats. The whole comparative connection is supplied. Scēaphierde is the nominative subject, scēap the accusative plural object, and gātum dative after fram. The noun scēap has identical singular/plural nominative/accusative shapes; the source explicitly identifies this occurrence as plural.

local_support.source_expression: gelōgað … on his swīðran hand … on his winstran
local_support.text: He places the sheep at his right hand and the goats at his left. Gelōgað is an exact supplied third-singular present. The two animal phrases are accusative plural objects. The right/left expressions share a placement frame; on takes accusative hand in this bounded right/left-side expression (the final hand is understood). The following unassigned source line8 uses the same expression with static standað; this is not a universal motion-versus-rest rule. Swīðran/winstran are weak feminine singular forms. Their -an alone does not distinguish accusative from dative; judge the complete clause and the bare hand form.

new_compositions.title: The stranger and the monk
new_compositions.text: Sum cuma cōm tō ðǣm giesthūse. Hine hyngrede, and hē wæs untrum. Ān ðāra munuca geseah ðone cuman. Se munuc sealde him męte and wæter. Se cuma cwæð: “Ðū ne forwiernst mē mętes.” Se munuc cwæð: “Ic fēde ðē gōde męte.” Se cuma ǣt ðone męte and dranc ðæt wæter.
new_compositions.target: Connected relief of hunger: impersonal experience, partitive identification, a gift, denial contrast and instrumental means. No private full translation is included.
new_compositions.support_policy: All required lexical senses, forms and constructions must be productive before this independent reading.

actual_prior_record.scope_note: No negative copula, contracted anomalous system, negative concord or untaught subordinate syntax.

actual_prior_record.description: Cuman means come in an ordinary intransitive clause and supplies the movement verb before the selected same-subject purpose infinitive.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: No unassigned destination phrase or sense of becuman follows.

actual_prior_record.description: Dōn means do/perform with an accusative work/thing in the selected elementary clauses, complements and commands.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: No causative, passive, perfect or arbitrary phrasal sense.

actual_prior_record.description: Second-singular commands address one person; plural commands address two or more, without a separate dual ending. The subject can remain unexpressed in the selected direct instructions.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: These are second-person commands, not third-person optative wishes or a new general politeness system.

actual_prior_record.description: Willan plus a plain infinitive expresses desire or willingness; wolde can state past desire without asserting that the desired act occurred.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Only the expressly selected forms, senses and constructions are assigned.

actual_prior_record.description: Nū now, swā so, ðus thus, ēac also and swilce likewise are invariant adverbs; efne behold introduces a statement as an interjection. Nū is may precede its nominal subject in the given presentational frame. The conjunction swilce as if is unassigned.

For assigned accusative-object verbs, present or preterite wesan/bēon or weorðan + past participle expresses passive. Finite auxiliary agrees with the nominative subject. Agent omitted in productive tasks; no new fram-agent rule needed. Wesan often presents state/result and weorðan event, but not an absolute contrast or one-to-one English tense mapping.
Promote eall strong NGDA and introduce image-checked longǣlc strong NGDA. Complete models do not teach unrelated indefinite pronouns, partitives, adverbial quantifier idioms or weak paradigms.
Divide waters from waters.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Only this selected lexical frame; no arbitrary case-government generalization.

actual_prior_record.description: Direct yes/no questions commonly begin with the finite verb; wh-words or phrases commonly precede the finite verb, and a wh-subject is itself the subject. No English dummy do is added. These are tendencies, not an exceptionless V2 transformation.

Ordinary attributive sum some/a certain, ǣnig any in questions, gehwilc each with singular noun, and swilc such; complete strong morphology. Following ordinary descriptive adjective in swilc phrases is strong. Extended negative/distributive/partitive/correlative constructions deferred.
Lexical hū how and hwȳ why in direct questions; hwȳ does not establish general instrumental syntax.
Question pronouns take the case their own function requires: subject nominative, possessor genitive, object accusative, recipient or governed dative.
Slēan may express making a stroke without naming an object.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Bounded ordinary striking use for the hammer; prior accusative-object construction is not erased.

actual_prior_record.description: Sęcgan can name its recipient in the dative with direct speech or a dependent content/question complement.
Mid + dative names an accompanying person or cargo.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Means/manner/abstract circumstance require their own prior or supplied records.

actual_prior_record.description: Complete present/preterite indicative systems of the seventeen explicitly selected new trade/narrative verbs.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: 204 cells. Citation infinitives do not license unassigned nonfinite production; wician plain infinitive is separately productive.

actual_prior_record.description: Gewyrcean may take an accusative object and an agreeing accusative predicate adjective.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Contrast prior hātan naming two-accusative construction; morphology must agree with the object, not the main subject.

actual_prior_record.description: Gesēon can take an accusative actor and a plain infinitive describing the perceived action.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: The actor belongs to the infinitival event; no claim that every verb takes this construction.

actual_prior_record.description: Behēfe useful takes a dative person to whom the subject is useful. The predicate adjective agrees with its subject, while the recipient noun is dative.
actual_prior_record.prior_status: The exact merchant clause was supplied in Unit8; ordinary productive useful+dative is new.

actual_prior_record.description: Ne + willan expresses unwillingness/refusal; translate the sense from context.
actual_prior_record.scope_note: Use prior positive forms with ne; no additional negative contraction paradigm or future auxiliary system assigned.
